28121.notes: Mississippi tax-lien county (Miss. Code §§27-41 et seq.). Rankin County Tax Collector sells delinquent real-property tax liens at the statutory last-Monday-in-August annual sale; documented cycles have used GovEase online live bidding (govease.com/auctions). Opening bid equals unpaid taxes plus costs; overbids are common and generally non-refundable on redemption (investor earns statutory interest on the tax amount only). Two-year redemption at 1.5%/month (18%/yr) through the Chancery Clerk Land Redemption desk before a tax deed can mature to the purchaser. Jackson metro east (Brandon, Flowood, Pearl, Ridgeland fringe).
28121.auctionFormat: Online (GovEase; confirm current cycle on county notices)

auctionPlatform.label: GovEase — Rankin County tax lien auction

28121.auctionFrequency: Annually, last Monday in August (runs multi-day until all parcels offered); registration typically opens ~last Monday in July on GovEase
28121.depositRules: Register on GovEase before the sale window; all deposits handled through GovEase (county offices do not take sale deposits). Credit-card convenience fees may apply and are not paid by the collector. Pay winning liens per GovEase settlement rules. Redemption of sold liens is handled at the Rankin County Chancery Clerk (no personal checks after July 1 on redemptions — cash/money order/certified funds).

taxCollector.label: Rankin County Tax Collector (annual tax sale)

clerkOfCourt.label: Rankin County Chancery Clerk — Land Redemption / Delinquent Tax

28121.survivingLiens: Certificate is a lien, not fee title. Owner has two years to redeem with 1.5%/mo interest. After tax deed matures post-redemption, most private liens are cut off, but federal tax liens can survive and MS tax titles are frequently litigated — verify notice quality before relying on the deed.
28121.quietTitle: Very commonly required in Mississippi for marketable/insurable tax title before resale; budget for quiet title after deed issuance.

42027.notes: Pennsylvania Real Estate Tax Sale Law (RETSL / 72 P.S. §5860) county. Centre County Tax Claim Bureau runs the annual Upset Sale for delinquent real estate taxes (typically September; 2025 Upset Sale was Sept 16, 2025 at Willowbank Office Building, Bellefonte). Upset purchasers take subject to many liens; unsold parcels may later go to Judicial Sale designed to free most properly notified liens. No classic post-sale redemption for most RETSL counties. Distinct from Centre County Sheriff mortgage sales. State College / Penn State metro.

auctionPlatform.label: Centre County Tax Claim Bureau — Upset / Judicial Sales

42027.depositRules: Pre-register ~10 days before the Upset Sale with $25 non-refundable fee (cash or check to Centre County Tax Claim Bureau) plus Bidder Affidavit (individual/corporate/LLC per Act 33 of 2021 guidance). No day-of registration. Payment of winning bids typically certified funds same day per Bureau conditions — read current Upset/Judicial Sale Conditions packet before registering.

42027.quietTitle: Judicial sale judgments often support marketable title; upset-sale purchasers frequently need a later judicial sale or quiet title to clear residual liens for insurance.

33013.notes: New Hampshire tax process is MUNICIPAL, not county-run (RSA Ch. 80). Merrimack County itself does not run a unified tax-deed auction. Concord (county seat / largest city) is the primary reference; also track Hooksett, Pembroke, Franklin, Bow, etc. separately.

35049.notes: New Mexico tax sales are NOT run by the county — the NM Taxation & Revenue Department Property Tax Division (PTD) conducts delinquent-property auctions statewide after collection efforts fail (~3-year delinquency threshold). Buyer receives a tax deed (not a lien certificate); only residual federal IRS 120-day redemption is noted by PTD. Confirm whether Santa Fe County parcels appear on the current PTD schedule before planning a trip — call PTD (505) 827-0883. County Assessor/Treasurer remain useful for parcel and current-tax research.

27139.notes: Minnesota tax-forfeiture deed county (Minn. Stat. Ch. 280–282). After statutory judgment and redemption periods, title forfeits to the State; Scott County Property & Taxation Services manages parcels in trust and classifies non-conservation land for public auction. County page directs subscribers to auction notifications; Public Surplus has hosted Scott County tax-forfeited real estate. Sold AS IS; special assessments canceled at forfeiture may be reassessed by municipalities (Minn. Stat. §429.071). Post-Tyler / statewide tax-forfeiture settlement surplus-claim process applies. Twin Cities south metro (Shakopee, Prior Lake, Savage, Elko New Market).

23019.notes: Maine municipal tax-lien foreclosure system (not a county-run auction). Each city/town files tax lien certificates; if unpaid ~18 months after filing, the lien automatically forecloses and the municipality owns the property (36 M.R.S. §943). Sale of tax-acquired property follows 36 M.R.S. §943-C (post-Tyler reforms): towns generally must use listed/broker processes and return surplus proceeds. Inventory and method (listing, sealed bid, occasional auction) vary by municipality. Bangor is the largest city and primary example; also track Brewer, Orono, Old Town, Millinocket, etc. Unorganized territory uses Maine Revenue Services broker process.

23019.depositRules: Follow each municipality's tax-acquired property sale notice for deposits, earnest money, and closing. Expect quitclaim/municipal deed without warranty. Budget survey, title insurance, and possible quiet title. Verify lien filing and foreclosure dates at Penobscot County Registry of Deeds.

34011.notes: New Jersey municipal tax-lien system (N.J.S.A. 54:5) — sales are by municipal tax collectors, not a county deed auction. Cumberland County municipalities (Vineland, Millville, Bridgeton, etc.) each hold at least one annual tax sale for delinquent taxes and municipal charges. Bidding typically reverse-auctions interest from 18% toward 0%, with premium possible at 0%. Certificate is not a deed; third-party holders generally wait 2 years then file Superior Court foreclosure of the right of redemption. Vineland is the largest municipality and primary example; platforms may include Bid4Assets or RealAuction/newjerseytaxsale.com — confirm each town's notice. County Sheriff mortgage sales are a separate product.

48397.notes: Texas redeemable-deed tax foreclosure county. Separate from 1st-Tuesday trustee/mortgage foreclosure sales on the courthouse steps (not tax). Confirm whether the current tax-sale cycle is online (Bid4Assets) or in-person with the Sheriff/constable and tax counsel before registering. Statutory redemption rights and high penalties apply under Tax Code Ch. 34. Fast-growing lakeside suburban market (Rockwall, Heath, Fate, Royse City).

54003.notes: West Virginia hybrid tax-lien / delinquent-land system centralized under the State Auditor's Office (W.Va. Code Ch. 11A; post-SB 552). County Sheriff certifies delinquencies; State Auditor County Collections runs the annual public land sale cycle for most counties including Berkeley. Pre-register once per year for all WV counties at wvsao.gov. After sale, statutory redemption period (~18 months class) before tax deed path. Berkeley County Sheriff Tax Office still handles local payment/redemption questions pre-certification. Eastern Panhandle / Martinsburg–I-81 growth market (DC/Baltimore commute fringe).

33017.notes: New Hampshire municipal tax system (RSA Ch. 80) — not county-run. Towns/cities take tax liens and may deed property after statutory waiting, then sell tax-deeded parcels via sealed bid, BidNet, auction, or listing under post-Tyler surplus rules. Strafford County itself does not run a tax sale. Dover is the largest city and has sold tax-deeded city property via sealed-bid solicitation (BidNet Direct historically); also track Rochester, Somersworth, Durham, Barrington, Farmington separately.

33017.depositRules: Per each municipality's tax-acquired property RFP/sale notice. Expect quitclaim deeds and surplus-proceeds compliance. Budget title insurance and possible quiet title. Verify chain at Strafford County Registry of Deeds.

16019.notes: Idaho tax-deed county (Idaho Code Title 63, Ch. 10). County takes tax deed administratively after ~3 years delinquency, then auctions surplus deeded property. Bonneville County Treasurer runs in-person public auctions in the Commissioners Hearing Room (605 N Capital Ave, Idaho Falls) when inventory is ready — no fixed annual date. May 13, 2026 tax sale was CANCELLED per county page; watch for next posted notice. No registration required to attend; sealed bids allowed only with prior Commissioners' approval. Payment in full day of sale. Idaho Falls metro / Snake River Plain.

16019.depositRules: No registration fee to attend. Payment in full day of sale: cash, cashier's check, money order, personal or bank check (deeds for verified funds no sooner than day after sale; non-verified funds subject to bank clearance). Unsold Regular Tax Sale items go to Adjourned Tax Sale in Treasurer Room 140 beginning the 3rd Monday of each subsequent month. 34019.notes: New Jersey municipal tax-lien county (N.J.S.A. 54:5). Raritan Township Tax Collector (largest municipality) states the office conducts annual tax sales. Format is typically reverse-interest bidding from 18%; certificate foreclosure is a separate Superior Court process after statutory wait. 05125.notes: Arkansas tax-deed system is STATE-run through the Commissioner of State Lands (COSL), not the county. County does not set deposit rules. Benton / Bryant / Hot Springs Village fringe — Little Rock southwest suburban growth market.

44009.notes: Rhode Island municipal redeemable-deed tax sales (R.I. Gen. Laws Ch. 44-9) — no active county government tax auction. Each city/town collector sells tax titles at public auction; 1-year redemption with 10% year-one penalty class plus monthly interest thereafter. Washington County (South County) towns include Westerly, South Kingstown, North Kingstown, Narragansett, Charlestown, Hopatcong-class peers Hopkinton, Richmond, Exeter. RI Tax Collectors Association lists staggered 2026 municipal sales (e.g. Westerly 4/7/2026; Union Fire District of South Kingstown 5/22/2026; Narragansett 10/15/2026). Track the specific town, not the county label.

44009.depositRules: Confirm deposit and payment (typically cash or certified funds day of sale) with the town collector and the published sale notice. Expect tax title subject to 1-year redemption. Budget quiet title for marketable title after redemption expires. Coastal flood, CRMC, and septic constraints are critical South County DD items.

44009.quietTitle: Often required for marketable title after a Rhode Island tax sale deed.
